answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bonded stake that acts as an anchor: every agent must lock a ferrous-hard deposit of tokens before proposing work, and peers slash it if the identity proves duplicated. A gale of fake accounts can multiply identities cheaply, but each copy must post the same costly bond, so attack cost grows linearly while honest stake stays singular.
